- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise sharply, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after supply shocks.  
- If true outcomes show strong mean reversion after a spike (e.g., 76+ → 70+), reduce forecast momentum by 10–15% in subsequent periods.  
- When official supply net is negative and bearish sentiment dominates, model should not overcorrect upward — adjust forecast downward by 2–5% relative to prior peak.  
- If model forecasts are flat or rising slowly while true outcomes show volatility (e.g., 70→76→70), introduce a 3–5 day lagged volatility buffer to capture event-driven swings.  
- For 30-day forecasts with high event count and negative supply net, reduce forecast mean by 3–7% relative to historical 30d average to account for policy-driven downward pressure.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model should not assume sustained trend — apply a 2–3 day smoothing filter to avoid overfitting sentiment.
